cards.explanation: The answer is Eat. Mark says the crowd gathered so that Jesus and His disciples "…could not even eat." (Mark 3:20). When I get that busy, it's because a batch is burning, and even then I grab a cookie. I think that's a LOT of people, friends.

The answer is His family. Mark 3:21 says that when His family heard about this, they went out to take custody of Him. The text tells us what they said, but it doesn't tell us why they said it, so I won't guess. I'll just say it's a tough moment, friends.

The answer is True. Mark 3:21 says His family went out to take custody of Him, saying, "He is out of His mind." That's a hard thing to hear about Jesus from the people closest to Him. I think this one stings a little.

The answer is the prince of the demons. The scribes who had come down from Jerusalem said, "By the prince of the demons He drives out demons." (Mark 3:22). They also said He was possessed by Beelzebul. That's quite a claim, friends, and Jesus is about to answer it.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "If a kingdom is divided against itself, it cannot stand." (Mark 3:24). Nothing in that line about being strong enough. When I try to bake with two cooks pulling the oven in opposite directions, nobody wins.

The answer is end. Jesus says, "And if Satan is divided and rises against himself, he cannot stand; his end has come." (Mark 3:26). He's answering the scribes' idea with a plain picture, friends. A divided side doesn't last.

The answer is that he ties up the strong man. Jesus says no one can enter a strong man's house to steal his possessions "…unless he first ties up the strong man." (Mark 3:27). The order matters: tie him up first, then the house. The text doesn't say more than that.

The answer is True. Jesus says no one can steal from the house unless he first ties up the strong man, and then adds, "Then he can plunder his house." (Mark 3:27). Tie him up first, and then the house. It's a short picture with a clear order, friends.

The answer is the Holy Spirit. Jesus says, "But whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin." (Mark 3:29). That's a serious line, friends. Mark tells us in verse 30 what was being said when Jesus spoke it.

The answer is True. Jesus says whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit "…will never be forgiven; he is guilty of eternal sin." (Mark 3:29). It follows His line that the sons of men will be forgiven all sins and blasphemies (Mark 3:28). Mark ties it to what was being said in verse 30 (Mark 3:30).

The answer is that they were saying, "He has an unclean spirit." Mark 3:30 says Jesus made this statement because they were saying that. The writer gives us the reason outright, friends, so we don't have to guess.

The answer is that He asks who His mother and brothers are. Jesus replies, "Who are My mother and My brothers?" (Mark 3:33). I think that question got the whole room's attention, friends. Then He looks at the people around Him.
The answer is False. Jesus looks at those seated in a circle around Him and says, "Here are My mother and My brothers!" (Mark 3:34). He calls them family, friends, and that's a warm thing to hear.

The answer is whoever does the will of God. Jesus says, "For whoever does the will of God is My brother and sister and mother." (Mark 3:35). That's the door He opens to anybody. I'd have taken that welcome back when I was stuck in a junk drawer, friends.
